items.caption: This oracle-script style redraw places a large enclosed, open-bottom form above a smaller figure whose side branches descend from a central junction. It illustrates one reported early layout of 好, but the shapes alone do not identify the components or settle the character’s original motivation.
items.alt: Black redraw with a large upper loop open at the bottom and a smaller lower figure with diagonal branches descending from a central junction.
items.selection_reason: The visible size contrast is relevant to the reported mother–child interpretation, while leaving the figures’ identities and original meaning unresolved.
items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern redraw, not a dated artifact specimen

items.caption: This bronze-script style redraw places an upright, forked figure on the left beside a rounded, mostly closed form on the right. It shows a contrasting arrangement of the two reported components, not a chronological stage after the oracle-style form.
items.alt: Black redraw with a tall forked figure on the left and a rounded, nearly closed form on the right.
items.selection_reason: Its arrangement helps illustrate reported variation in the relative placement of 女 and 子; the redraw is not a dated inscription specimen.
items.period: Bronze-script style; no specific specimen date established

limitations.text: 好’s original motivation remains unresolved. Proposed explanations include mother–child affection, a woman’s beauty, and affection between a man and a woman; cited early uses do not directly attest the mother–child interpretation.
These are modern redrawings labeled by script tradition, not photographs of dated inscriptions. Their labels do not establish a specimen date or a chronological sequence between the forms.
